values.title: Bright Scarf Slow Track
values.objective: Support slow visual tracking with a bright moving scarf.
values.description: Baby watches a large bright scarf move slowly across their view while you name the color in a calm voice.
values.preparation:
Choose one high-contrast bright color
Clear visual clutter behind you
values.setup: Place baby comfortably on back or supported side on a mat.
values.steps:
1. Settle baby and gain eye contact first
2. Hold scarf about 8–12 inches away
3. Move slowly left, pause, then right
4. Name the color once or twice
5. Stop when baby looks away
values.teacherLanguage: Look… see the bright red? Watching… watching.
values.observationOpportunities: Tracks scarf briefly; stays calm while looking.
values.safetyNotes: Keep scarf away from face/neck; never leave draped on baby.
values.ageModifications: Infant 0–6 months (younger: look only; older: may bat scarf)

values.title: Tummy Color Mirror Look
values.objective: Combine tummy time with mirror looking and a color accent.
values.description: Baby does short tummy time facing a baby-safe mirror with one colorful cloth beside it.
values.preparation: Angle mirror for baby’s face view
values.setup: Mirror at edge of mat; cloth to the side — not covering mirror.
values.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Point to baby’s face in mirror
3. Show cloth briefly beside mirror
4. Talk about looking
5. Rest on back
values.teacherLanguage: I see you! And soft blue beside you.

values.title: Shaded Color Stroll
values.objective: Notice real-world colors outdoors with caregiver pointing and talk.
values.description: In shade, you stroll or sit outdoors and point to large colorful things (flowers, balls, clothing) while narrating.
values.materials:
Stroller or outdoor blanket
Sun protection as needed
values.steps:
1. Settle baby facing out or toward you
2. Point to one colorful object
3. Name color and object
4. Pause for looking
5. Return indoors before overstimulation/heat
values.teacherLanguage: See the yellow flower? Bright outside.
values.observationOpportunities: Looks toward pointed object; stays content outdoors.
values.safetyNotes: Shade, hydration for adults, never leave stroller unattended; follow safe sleep if nap begins.

values.title: High-Contrast Card Focus
values.objective: Support visual focus with one bold black-and-white card.
values.description: Baby looks at a single high-contrast card held 8–12 inches away while you describe the pattern.
values.preparation:
Select one simple pattern (stripes or bullseye)
Sit facing baby
values.setup: Baby comfortable on mat; card ready.
values.steps:
1. Hold card steady in view
2. Allow time to focus
3. Move slightly side to side
4. Name pattern simply (stripes/spots)
5. Rest eyes
values.safetyNotes: Sealed laminate edges; no glitter/loose parts.

values.title: Tummy Contrast Gallery
values.objective: Offer 2 contrast visuals during tummy time without clutter.
values.description: Two cards stand along the mat edge like a tiny gallery while baby does tummy time.
values.materials:
2 cards or tummy strip
Mat
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
Printable (draft): Tummy-Time Visual Strip
values.preparation:
Space cards apart
Sit opposite baby
values.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Tap lightly near one card to invite look
3. Shift attention to second card
4. Return to face-to-face
5. Rest

values.title: Shade and Shadow Contrast Stroll
values.objective: Notice natural light/dark contrast outdoors with caregiver talk.
values.description: In safe shade, point out shadows and bright/dark areas while strolling or sitting.
values.materials:
Stroller or blanket
Optional contrast card
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
values.steps:
1. Settle baby
2. Point to shadow/light area
3. Describe dark and light
4. Optional show card in outdoor light
5. Return inside
values.observationOpportunities: Looks toward pointed contrast; content outdoors.
values.safetyNotes: Shade; supervision; safe sleep if drowsy.

values.title: Community Helper Discovery Basket
values.objective: Explore helper props and photos to build job vocabulary.
values.description: Children examine hats, tools, and helper cards from a basket and talk about who uses them.
values.materials:
Basket
Assorted helper props
Helper picture cards (printable)
Printable (draft): Community Helper Picture Cards
values.preparation:
Fill basket with safe props from many jobs
Include diverse helper images
values.setup: Circle or small-group basket at child height.
values.steps:
1. Pull one item and wonder aloud who might use it
2. Invite children to try hats/props
3. Match a prop to a helper card if they choose
4. Share which helper they want to play today
5. Return props to basket
values.teacherLanguage: Who might use this tool? What job helps our community?
values.observationOpportunities: Names helpers; matches tool to role; handles props safely.
values.safetyNotes: No sharp tools; supervise small props.

values.title: Grocery Helper Market
values.objective: Role-play grocery helpers who stock, shop, and help customers.
values.description: Children run a market: stockers, cashiers, baggers, and shoppers using play food.
values.materials:
Play food
Baskets
Register/clipboard
Shelves
Market sign
Printable (draft): Helper Place Signs
values.preparation:
Stock shelves messily so children can restock
Price tags optional
values.steps:
1. Choose a market job
2. Stock or shop with a list (picture list OK)
3. Practice kind customer talk
4. Bag groceries
5. Rotate jobs
values.teacherLanguage: How can a grocery helper make shopping easier?
values.observationOpportunities: Uses job talk; sorts food; cooperates.
values.safetyNotes: No real glass containers; allergy-aware pretend foods.

values.title: Community Helpers Celebration
values.objective: Review favorite helpers and celebrate with thank-you chant.
values.description: Class reviews the week’s helpers, shares favorites, and sings Thank You Helpers Chant.
values.materials:
Helper cards
Thank-you basket of cards
Song chart
Printable (draft): Community Helper Picture Cards
values.steps:
1. Recall helpers from the week
2. Share a favorite
3. Show thank-you art basket
4. Sing chant
5. Send family connection reminder
values.teacherLanguage: Which helper are you thankful for today?
values.observationOpportunities: Recalls roles; participates in chant; gratitude talk.

values.title: Weather Watchers Circle
values.objective: Observe outdoors/window weather and record it on the class chart.
values.description: Children look outside, describe sky/air, and place a weather symbol on today’s chart square.
values.materials:
Weather chart
Symbol cards (printable)
Window/door access
Printable (draft): Weather Symbol Cards
Printable (draft): Weekly Weather Observation Chart
values.preparation:
Post chart at child height
Prep today’s blank square
values.steps:
1. Look outside together
2. Share what you notice (sky, wet, wind)
3. Choose a weather symbol
4. Mark warm/cool with a simple choice
5. Predict tomorrow in one word
values.teacherLanguage: What do you observe about today’s weather?
values.observationOpportunities: Describes weather; places symbol; uses weather words.

values.title: Thunder Drum Experiment
values.objective: Explore loud/soft storm sounds safely and talk about storm feelings/safety.
values.description: Children compare drum/pan sounds as ‘thunder’ play, then practice calm-down and indoor-safety talk.
values.materials:
Drums
Metal pans
Mallets
Soft scarves for calm-down
values.preparation:
Warn sensitive children
Offer quiet corner
values.steps:
1. Practice soft taps
2. Try louder taps (still safe)
3. Compare which sounds like far/near thunder
4. Talk storm safety (go indoors)
5. Calm with slow breathing and scarves
values.teacherLanguage: Thunder is loud — what helps your body feel safe?
values.observationOpportunities: Controls volume; discusses feelings; recalls safety.
values.safetyNotes: Ear-aware; no banging near faces; stop if distressed.

values.title: Weather Watchers Celebration
values.objective: Review the week’s weather data and celebrate investigations.
values.description: Class counts chart data, thanks chart helpers, sings, and shares favorite activities.
values.materials:
Completed chart
Song list
Optional photos of investigations
Printable (draft): Weather Symbol Cards
Printable (draft): Weekly Weather Observation Chart
values.steps:
1. Count weather types for the week
2. Thank chart helpers
3. Sing Weather Watchers Song
4. Share favorite investigation
5. Send family weather-watch reminder
values.teacherLanguage: What weather did we see most this week?
